Use it for\\\\n  alarms on AWS/EBS metrics (VolumeReadOps, VolumeWriteOps, VolumeReadBytes,\\\\n  VolumeWriteBytes, VolumeQueueLength, VolumeTotalReadTime/WriteTime,\\\\n  VolumeAvgReadLatency, VolumeStalledIOCheck, BurstBalance) or\\\\n  EBSIOBalance%/EBSByteBalance%; for sizing\\\\n  IOPS or throughput changes; for requests to raise IOPS or modify a volume; for a\\\\n  volume modification that looks stuck or failed; for deciding which snapshots or\\\\n  AMIs need owner review before deletion, or how to recover them; for KMS errors\\\\n  on encrypted volumes; for EBS quota or limit errors; for a jump in the EBS bill;\\\\n  and for a pre-launch EBS review. Do not use it for S3, EFS, FSx, instance store,\\\\n  or EC2 problems unrelated to EBS.\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  author: dewavic\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  summary: \\\\\"Troubleshoot Amazon EBS performance, volume modifications, snapshots, encryption, quotas and cost, and review an account\\'s EBS setup with read-only checks.\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"CHAT, INCIDENT_RCA\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon EBS, Amazon EC2, Amazon CloudWatch, AWS CloudTrail, AWS Service Quotas\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"Storage\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n# Amazon EBS Expertise\\\\n\\\\nUse this skill to troubleshoot Amazon EBS problems and to review an account\\'s Amazon EBS setup. It has two modes. Troubleshoot mode answers \\\\\"something is wrong, why?\\\\\" through one of five paths and returns a fixed verdict. Review mode answers \\\\\"is my EBS setup healthy before something goes wrong?\\\\\" and returns a rated report. Both modes are read-only and share the same volume-type rules, instance limits and service rules. Load only the reference files the request needs.\\\\n\\\\n## When to Use This Skill\\\\n\\\\n- Storage-related slowness, timeouts or high I/O latency on an Amazon EC2 instance.\\\\n- An alarm on AWS/EBS metrics or on instance `EBSIOBalance%` / `EBSByteBalance%`.\\\\n- A request to raise IOPS or throughput, or to modify a volume.\\\\n- A volume modification that looks stuck, failed, or did not improve performance.\\\\n- Snapshot, AMI, Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager, AWS Backup or Recycle Bin questions, including which snapshots need owner review before deletion.\\\\n- Encrypted-volume access errors and AWS KMS questions for Amazon EBS.\\\\n- Amazon EBS cost increases, idle or over-provisioned volumes.\\\\n- An operation that failed on an Amazon EBS quota, or \\\\\"how close am I to my limits?\\\\\"\\\\n- A request to review Amazon EBS posture before a launch, migration or peak event.\\\\n\\\\nDo not use this skill for Amazon S3, Amazon EFS, Amazon FSx, instance store, or Amazon EC2 issues unrelated to Amazon EBS.\\\\n\\\\n## Prerequisites\\\\n\\\\n- Read-only permissions for the APIs listed in [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md).\\\\n- AWS CloudTrail access is optional. The skill works without it.\\\\n- Mutating changes run only through directed actions (Agent Actions in the Operator Web App), which need their own role and operator approval on the approval card.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Workflow\\\\n\\\\nCopy this checklist and tick each step as you finish it:\\\\n\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Classify the request\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Load the shared references\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: Run the path and draft the report\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: Check the draft, fix it, then present it\\\\n\\\\n## Step 1: Classify the Request\\\\n\\\\n| The user says or the alarm shows | Mode and path | Load |\\\\n|---|---|---|\\\\n| \\\\\"My app is slow\\\\\", high latency, an alarm on AWS/EBS metrics, `EBSIOBalance%` or `EBSByteBalance%`, \\\\\"is it storage?\\\\\", \\\\\"how much IOPS do I need?\\\\\" | Troubleshoot: performance | [references/troubleshoot-performance.md](references/troubleshoot-performance.md) |\\\\n| \\\\\"My modification is stuck\\\\\", \\\\\"the new IOPS has not taken effect\\\\\", a `ModifyVolume` error, resize, gp2 to gp3, extend the file system, shrink or cancel | Troubleshoot: volume modification | [references/troubleshoot-volume-modification.md](references/troubleshoot-volume-modification.md) |\\\\n| \\\\\"Which snapshots can I delete?\\\\\", snapshot copy did not arrive, AMI creation stuck, recover a deleted snapshot or volume, Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager, Recycle Bin | Troubleshoot: snapshots | [references/troubleshoot-snapshots.md](references/troubleshoot-snapshots.md) |\\\\n| [references/review-operational.md](references/review-operational.md) and [references/review-report-format.md](references/review-report-format.md) |\\\\n\\\\nIf a request fits more than one row, answer the question the user asked first and treat the rest as Separate findings.\\\\n\\\\n## Step 2: Load the Shared References\\\\n\\\\n- Always load [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md) (read-only APIs, metric math, errors and fallbacks).\\\\n- Load [references/metrics-thresholds.md](references/metrics-thresholds.md) for any metric judgement.\\\\n- Load [references/finding-logic.md](references/finding-logic.md) for the verdict, the binding layer, escalation and review ratings.\\\\n- Load [references/ebs-best-practices.md](references/ebs-best-practices.md) for service rules (Elastic Volumes, instance limits, quotas, snapshots, quirks).\\\\n\\\\n## Step 3: Run the Path and Draft the Report\\\\n\\\\nFollow the numbered procedure in the loaded path. Discover every value from the APIs. Then draft the report in the format below.\\\\n\\\\n### Troubleshoot verdict format\\\\n\\\\n1. **Answer:** the asked question, answered first.\\\\n2. **Evidence:** values with units and time window.\\\\n3. **Binding layer:** Volume, Instance, Burst credits, Quota, Not EBS, AWS-side impairment (only with a direct signal, see [references/finding-logic.md](references/finding-logic.md)), Indeterminate, or Not applicable.\\\\n4. **Recommendation:** exact parameters, or \\\\\"No change\\\\\".\\\\n5. **Separate findings:** other true facts that do not change the Answer.\\\\n6. **Gaps:** what could not be checked and why.\\\\n\\\\nIn an investigation, put the Answer and the Recommendation with its exact parameters in the root cause finding, not only under Gaps. Keep the findings on the resource the user asked about. Mention another volume only when it shares the same instance EBS baseline, and then as a Separate finding.\\\\n\\\\nWhen the Binding layer is Indeterminate, report it as one finding. Do not offer AWS-side impairment as a hypothesis. List each direct check you ran (volume status, `VolumeStalledIOCheck`, AWS Health, AWS FIS) with its result as supporting evidence, say that no check confirms or rules out an EBS-side slowdown, and give the escalation path.\\\\n\\\\nReview mode uses the rated report in [references/review-report-format.md](references/review-report-format.md). Every Review mode response MUST begin with its Summary table, which rates all six areas (capacity and quota headroom, observability, cost hygiene, resilience, encryption posture, deletion protection), even when an area has no findings or is `Indeterminate`. The Summary table is required, not optional. Do not open with prose or an offer to run the review; start with the table, then the per-area detail.\\\\n\\\\n## Step 4: Check the Draft Before Presenting It\\\\n\\\\nReview the draft from Step 3 against these checks. Fix anything that fails, then present it.\\\\n\\\\n- Every number under Evidence came from an API call made in this session, has its unit and time window, and matches the resource ID it is attributed to.\\\\n- The Binding layer agrees with the Evidence: the named layer is the one at its limit, and the other layers were checked and shown to have headroom. The Evidence gives the instance EBS baseline in MiB/s and IOPS next to the summed demand of all attached volumes.\\\\n- Any Recommendation stays within the instance\\'s EBS baseline and the volume type\\'s documented limits, and it is not more provisioning for an impairment.\\\\n- Every snapshot tier is backed by the checks it requires; if one of those checks failed, the item is not listed for owner review. No snapshot is recommended for deletion; the owner confirms first.\\\\n- A review answer starts with the Summary table and rates all six areas.\\\\n- Every API that failed or was not called is listed under Gaps.\\\\n\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n## Critical Rules\\\\n\\\\n- **Read-only.** Changes (ModifyVolume, quota requests) are proposed with exact parameters, cost and rollback, and run only through operator-approved directed actions (Agent Actions in the Operator Web App). Approval is given only on the approval card. A typed \\\\\"approve\\\\\" in chat is not approval.\\\\n- **Deletes are manual customer steps.** AWS DevOps Agent refuses delete-class operations (for example DeleteSnapshot, DeleteVolume, DeregisterImage), so never propose them as directed actions. After the owner confirms they no longer need the resource, give the commands for the customer to run with their own credentials.\\\\n- **Answer in one reply.** In chat, run the checks in this conversation and return the finished verdict or report as your reply. Do not hand the work to a background sub-agent and reply with a \\\\\"started\\\\\" or \\\\\"I will report back\\\\\" message, because that message becomes the answer the user sees first.\\\\n- **Discover, don\\'t assume:** read every configuration value from the APIs.\\\\n- **Rule EBS in or out before tuning it.**\\\\n- **Answer the asked question first;** other findings go under \\\\\"Separate findings\\\\\".\\\\n- **Review mode starts with the Summary table.** Every Review mode response begins with the Summary table of all six rated areas. The table is required, not optional.\\\\n- **Always check the instance layer** and size changes within the instance\\'s EBS **baseline**.\\\\n- **Never recommend more provisioning for an impairment.**\\\\n- **Use current service rules:** up to 4 Elastic Volumes modifications per volume per rolling 24 hours. There is no fixed waiting period between modifications; the next one is allowed once the previous one completes.\\\\n- **No interpretation without data:** report what couldn\\'t be checked and use fallbacks. `DescribeVolumesModifications` returns only the most recent modification per volume; modification history and counts come from the optional AWS CloudTrail `ModifyVolume` events, or are listed under Gaps.\\\\n- **Units:** MiB/s for throughput, stated every time.\\\\n- **Escalate** on scope signals or when the investigation can\\'t explain the symptom.\\\\n\\\\n## Gotchas\\\\n\\\\n- A modification in `optimizing` is not stuck. The new size, IOPS or throughput already applies while it optimizes.\\\\n- `DescribeInstanceTypes` reports EBS bandwidth in MB/s. Convert it to MiB/s before comparing it with volume throughput.\\\\n- On io1 and io2, `VolumeThroughputPercentage` is the percentage of provisioned IOPS delivered. It is not a throughput signal.\\\\n- `VolumeAvgIOPS`, `VolumeAvgThroughput`, `VolumeAvgReadLatency` and `VolumeAvgWriteLatency` need both `VolumeId` and `InstanceId` and exist only on Nitro instances. `VolumeAvgThroughput` is in KiB/s. `VolumeTotalReadTime` and `VolumeTotalWriteTime` are in seconds.\\\\n- Rising latency and queue length with falling IOPS is not proof of an AWS-side impairment. Without a direct signal (failed `VolumeStalledIOCheck`, impaired volume status, or an open AWS Health event) and without a running AWS FIS experiment, the Binding layer is Indeterminate.\\\\n- `DescribeVolumesModifications` returns only the latest modification per volume. It cannot count modifications in the last 24 hours.\\\\n- `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` without `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true also lists snapshots that AWS Backup did not create.\\\\n- A snapshot whose source volume is gone may be the only remaining copy of the data. List it for owner review; never call it safe to delete.\\\\n- Snapshots are incremental, so deleting one may free less storage than its size suggests.\\\\n\\\\n## Error Handling\\\\n\\\\nErrors, gated reads and missing metrics are handled with the fallback table in [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md). {"id": "21a91224-670f-4e25-821d-b38a687f6afd", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_M4m6LHNiXliPlER9VUDjkm", "content": "[{'text': '# Troubleshoot: Elastic Volumes modification\\n\\n## When this path applies\\n\\n- \"My modification is stuck\", \"the new IOPS has not taken effect\", \"how long will optimizing take?\"\\n- A `ModifyVolume` call failed with an error.\\n- Sizing a resize, an IOPS or throughput change, or a gp2 to gp3 migration.\\n- Extending the file system after a size increase.\\n- Shrinking a volume or cancelling a modification.\\n\\n## Procedure\\n\\n1. **Find the volume.** Use the volume ID the user gives, or discover it with `DescribeVolumes` (by instance attachment or by the volumes that have recent modifications). Never pick a volume by its Name tag alone; confirm the ID with the user if more than one matches.\\n2. **Read the latest modification record.** `DescribeVolumesModifications` for the volume: `ModificationState`, `Progress`, original and target values (size, type, IOPS, throughput), `StartTime`, `EndTime`, `StatusMessage`. This API returns only the most recent modification request for each volume. Use it for the current or latest modification state, not for history.\\n3. **Answer the asked question first, in plain words.**\\n   - `modifying` or `optimizing`: not stuck. In `optimizing` the new configuration already applies and performance is between the source and the target. It completes on its own.\\n   - `completed`: done. The new values apply.\\n   - `failed`: read `StatusMessage` and translate it (step 5).\\n   - Duration is best effort. The Amazon EBS User Guide says a 1 TiB volume typically takes up to about six hours to modify, and some performance changes take more than 24 hours, for example when the volume is not fully initialized.\\n4. **Count the modifications in the rolling 24 hours.** Up to 4 per volume in a rolling 24-hour period. There is no fixed waiting period between modifications; the next one is allowed once the previous one completes. `DescribeVolumesModifications` cannot give this count, because it returns only the latest modification. Count the `ModifyVolume` events for the volume in the last 24 hours with the optional AWS CloudTrail `LookupEvents` call (filter on the volume ID as the resource name, or on the event name `ModifyVolume`). Report how many remain in the current window. As a cross-check, the latest record from step 2 should appear among those events if its `StartTime` is in the last 24 hours. If the lookup is denied or unavailable, record a Gap (\"the number of modifications in the last 24 hours could not be confirmed\") and do not state how many remain.\\n5. **Translate errors.**\\n   - io2 \"Iops to volume size ratio of ... is too high; maximum is 1000\": io2 allows up to 1,000 IOPS per GiB. To reach the target IOPS, the size must be at least target IOPS / 1,000 GiB. Propose that size together with the IOPS.\\n   - gp3: up to 500 IOPS per GiB, and throughput up to 0.25 MiB/s per provisioned IOPS. If a request breaks either rule, give the size or IOPS that satisfies it.\\n   - Size decrease: not allowed. Size can only increase. To get a smaller volume, create a new volume and copy the data.\\n   - Cancel: a submitted modification cannot be cancelled. Wait for it to complete; a reverse change then counts toward the 4 in 24 hours.\\n   - Limit reached: the 4 modifications in the window are used. The next one is possible when the oldest falls out of the rolling 24-hour window.\\n   - Older instance types or MBR volumes: check the Elastic Volumes requirements page.\\n6. **Size a new target.**\\n   - Keep it within the instance\\'s remaining EBS baseline: `DescribeInstanceTypes` baseline (converted to MiB/s) minus the measured usage of the other attached volumes.\\n   - gp2 to gp3: keep at least the gp2 volume\\'s current baseline IOPS (3 x GiB, minimum 100) and its measured throughput. gp3 includes 3,000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s at any size; provision more only if measured demand needs it.\\n   - State how the target was computed.\\n7. **File system extension after a size increase.** Give the commands for the operator to run on the instance. Never execute them.\\n   - `lsblk` to see the device and partition\\n   - `sudo growpart /dev/<device> <partition-number>` if the volume has a partition\\n   - `sudo xfs_growfs -d <mount-point>` for XFS, or `sudo resize2fs /dev/<device-or-partition>` for ext4\\n   - Point to the extend-the-file-system guide for Windows and other cases.\\n8. **Separate findings.** If the instance caps what the volume can deliver, write that under Separate findings. Never phrase it as \"the modification failed\" when the record shows `optimizing` or `completed`.\\n\\n## Decision rules\\n\\n- The modification record decides the Answer. Performance metrics never override it.\\n- An instance ceiling is a Separate finding with its own recommendation (instance type change).\\n- Use the binding-layer tree in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md) only when the user also asks about performance.\\n\\n## What to report\\n\\nThe verdict template in [finding-logic.md](finding-logic.md). The Answer names the state and what it means. Evidence lists the record fields. Recommendation gives the exact next call, if any. Gaps list anything unreadable.\\n\\n## Safety rules\\n\\n- The agent never runs `ModifyVolume` on its own. It proposes it as a directed action, approved on the approval card. A typed \"approve\" in chat is not approval.\\n- The proposal includes: the exact call (`--volume-id`, and only the changed fields among `--size`, `--volume-type`, `--iops`, `--throughput`), the expected state sequence (`modifying`, `optimizing`, `completed`), how many of the 4 modifications in the rolling 24 hours remain after this change (only when step 4 confirmed the count; otherwise say it is unconfirmed), cost direction, and rollback.\\n- Rollback: after the change completes, a reverse change of IOPS, throughput or type is possible and counts toward the 4. The agent gives the commands; the operator runs them.\\n- Read the requirements page before proposing a change on an older instance, or on a volume with an MBR partition (2 TiB limit).\\n\\n## Instance EBS layer\\n\\n- All volumes attached to an instance share the instance\\'s EBS bandwidth, IOPS and throughput. Sum the measured values across all attached volumes, including the root volume.\\n- Size any target within the instance\\'s EBS baseline from `DescribeInstanceTypes`, not its burst maximum.\\n- `DescribeInstanceTypes` reports throughput in MB/s at 128 KiB I/O and IOPS at 16 KiB I/O. Convert MB/s to MiB/s before comparing with volume throughput.\\n- Some smaller instance sizes burst above the baseline for a limited time and publish `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%`. When those balances drain or reach 0, the instance drops to its baseline.\\n\\n## Quotas\\n\\n- Amazon EBS quotas are per Region. A request within the per-volume maximum can still fail on the regional quota. Existing io2 volumes already consume part of that quota.\\n- Adjustable quotas are raised through Service Quotas. Quotas that are not adjustable need an AWS Support case.\\n\\n## Snapshots\\n\\n- Snapshots are incremental. Deleting a snapshot might not reduce storage cost, because later snapshots can reference its blocks. Any savings figure is an upper bound.\\n- You cannot delete a snapshot that is the root device snapshot of a registered AMI, even if the AMI is deprecated or disabled. Deregister the AMI first, and only if it is no longer needed.\\n- Snapshots created by AWS Backup are managed in AWS Backup, not with Amazon EC2 delete calls.\\n- Identify Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager snapshots by `aws:dlm:*` tags, never by the snapshot name or description. A snapshot can be named like a DLM snapshot and still have no `aws:dlm:*` tags.\\n- Target tags for Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager policies are case sensitive.\\n- Recycle Bin rules decide whether a deleted snapshot can be recovered. With no matching rule, deletion is permanent.\\n\\n## Quirks that change answers\\n\\n| Quirk | Rule |\\n|---|---|\\n| `VolumeThroughputPercentage` on io1/io2 | Reports the percentage of provisioned IOPS delivered. Not a throughput signal |\\n| `VolumeAvg*` metrics | Need `VolumeId` and `InstanceId`; Nitro only; `VolumeAvgThroughput` is KiB/s |\\n| Change history | `DescribeVolumesModifications` returns only the most recent modification request per volume. Tags are used for naming only, never as the source of a configuration value.\\n\\n## Read-only API allowlist\\n\\n| Service | APIs |\\n|---|---|\\n| Amazon EC2 | `DescribeVolumes`, `DescribeVolumeStatus`, `DescribeVolumesModifications`, `DescribeVolumeAttribute`, `DescribeInstances`, `DescribeInstanceTypes`, `DescribeInstanceAttribute`, `DescribeSnapshots`, `DescribeSnapshotAttribute`, `DescribeImages`, `DescribeFastSnapshotRestores`, `GetEbsEncryptionByDefault`, `GetEbsDefaultKmsKeyId`, `GetSnapshotBlockPublicAccessState`, `DescribeLockedSnapshots` |\\n| Amazon CloudWatch | `DescribeAlarms`, `DescribeAlarmHistory`, `GetMetricData`, `ListMetrics` |\\n| Service Quotas | `ListServiceQuotas`, `GetServiceQuota`, `GetAWSDefaultServiceQuota`, `ListRequestedServiceQuotaChangeHistoryByQuota` |\\n| Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager | `GetLifecyclePolicies`, `GetLifecyclePolicy` |\\n| Recycle Bin | `ListRules`, `GetRule` |\\n| AWS Backup | `ListBackupPlans`, `ListBackupSelections`, `GetBackupSelection`, `ListRecoveryPointsByResource` (always with `ManagedByAWSBackupOnly` set to true; without it the call also returns snapshots AWS Backup did not create), `ListProtectedResources` |\\n| AWS KMS | `DescribeKey`, `GetKeyPolicy`, `ListGrants` |\\n| AWS Cost Explorer | `GetCostAndUsage`, `GetDimensionValues` |\\n| AWS FIS | `ListExperiments`, `GetExperiment` |\\n| AWS Health | `DescribeEvents` |\\n| AWS Compute Optimizer (optional) | `GetEBSVolumeRecommendations` |\\n| AWS CloudTrail (optional) | `LookupEvents`. This call is optional. If it is denied or returns nothing, record a Gap and continue. Never make it a required step |\\n\\nNothing outside this list is called by the skill on its own. Mutating calls are proposals (see SKILL.md Critical rules).\\n\\n## Metric rules\\n\\nAWS/EBS publishes 1-minute data.\\n\\n| Namespace | Metrics | Dimensions |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| AWS/EBS | `VolumeAvgIOPS` (Ops/s), `VolumeAvgThroughput` (KiB/s), `VolumeAvgReadLatency` (milliseconds), `VolumeAvgWriteLatency` (milliseconds), `VolumeStalledIOCheck` (0 passed, 1 failed) | `VolumeId` AND `InstanceId`. Nitro instances only |\\n| AWS/EBS | `VolumeReadOps`, `VolumeWriteOps`, `VolumeReadBytes`, `VolumeWriteBytes`, `VolumeTotalReadTime` (seconds), `VolumeTotalWriteTime` (seconds), `VolumeQueueLength`, `VolumeIdleTime` (seconds), `BurstBalance`, `VolumeThroughputPercentage` (Provisioned IOPS SSD only) | `VolumeId` |\\n| AWS/EC2 | `EBSIOBalance%`, `EBSByteBalance%`, `EBSReadOps`, `EBSWriteOps`, `EBSReadBytes`, `EBSWriteBytes` | `InstanceId` |\\n\\nMetric math from the Amazon CloudWatch metrics page for Amazon EBS. Use `Sum` statistics for ops, bytes and time.\\n\\n- IOPS = Sum(`VolumeReadOps` + `VolumeWriteOps`) / period in seconds\\n- MiB/s = Sum(`VolumeReadBytes` + `VolumeWriteBytes`) / period in seconds / 1,048,576\\n- Average read latency in milliseconds per operation = Sum(`VolumeTotalReadTime`, in seconds) / Sum(`VolumeReadOps`) x 1,000 (and the write equivalent with `VolumeTotalWriteTime` and `VolumeWriteOps`). Without the x 1,000 the result is in seconds. Always state latency in milliseconds\\n- Idle percentage = Sum(`VolumeIdleTime`) / period in seconds x 100\\n- MiB/s from `VolumeAvgThroughput` = value in KiB/s / 1,024\\n\\nWhat a 1-minute average hides: sub-minute peaks can reach a limit while the minute average looks below it (micro-bursting). When latency or queue length rises while the average sits below the limit, say that headroom is not proven instead of claiming it.\\n\\n`EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%` are published only for some instance sizes (generally 4xlarge and smaller) that can burst. If they are absent, the instance does not publish them. That is not a fault.\\n\\n## Errors and fallbacks\\n\\n| What happens | What it means | What to do |\\n|---|---|---|\\n| `AccessDenied` on any call | The role cannot read that data | Name the exact API in Gaps. Continue with the rest |\\n| A read call is held behind an operator-approval gate (for example `dlm:GetLifecyclePolicies` or `rbin:ListRules`) | The Agent Space treats it as an action | Report it as a Gap and say which conclusion stays unconfirmed. Never ask the operator to bypass the gate |\\n| No `VolumeAvg*` data | The instance is not Nitro, or the `InstanceId` dimension is missing | Add `InstanceId`. If still empty, use the Sum-based math above |\\n| `EBSIOBalance%` absent | The instance size does not publish it | Compare the summed IOPS and MiB/s of all attached volumes to the `DescribeInstanceTypes` baseline |\\n| `DescribeInstanceTypes` values in MB/s | The API reports instance throughput in MB/s (bandwidth in Mbps) | Convert to MiB/s before comparing (1 MB/s = 1,000,000 bytes/s; 1 MiB/s = 1,048,576 bytes/s) |\\n| AWS CloudTrail optional lookup denied or empty | No access, or the event is older than the 90 days that `LookupEvents` covers | Use `DescribeVolumesModifications` for the current or latest modification only; it returns only the most recent modification per volume. Record a Gap for the modification history and for the 24-hour modification count |\\n| No metric data for a volume | The volume is new, detached, or the window is wrong | Check `DescribeVolumes` state and attachment times, widen the window, report the Gap |\\n\\n## Sources\\n\\n- Amazon CloudWatch metrics for Amazon EBS (units, dimensions, `VolumeStalledIOCheck` with `VolumeId` and `InstanceId`, and the latency formula Sum(`VolumeTotalReadTime`) / Sum(`VolumeReadOps`) x 1000 in ms/op): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/using_cloudwatch_ebs.html\\n- Instance metrics, including `EBSIOBalance%` and `EBSByteBalance%`: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/viewing_metrics_with_cloudwatch.html\\n- Amazon EBS-optimized instances (baseline and maximum, MB/s): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ebs-optimized.html\\n- Monitoring volume modifications: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/monitoring-volume-modifications.html\\n- DescribeVolumesModifications (most recent modification request only): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/APIReference/API_DescribeVolumesModifications.html\\n- AWS CloudTrail LookupEvents (last 90 days): https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/APIReference/API_LookupEvents.html\\n- AWS FIS actions: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fis/latest/userguide/fis-actions-reference.html\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "7dabe9f6-e830-4ae6-8ff5-c5d5b2eeac3e", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "**Your 15 GiB io2 volume can't hold 20,000 IOPS, so the request was rejected. The fix is to raise the size to at least 20 GiB, or lower the IOPS to 15,000 or less.**

**Why it failed**
- io2 allows at most 1,000 provisioned IOPS per GiB of volume size.
- 20,000 IOPS on 15 GiB is a ratio of 1,333.3, which is over that limit.
- At 15 GiB the most you can provision is 15,000 IOPS (15 × 1,000).
- To reach 20,000 IOPS, the volume needs at least 20,000 ÷ 1,000 = 20 GiB.
- The request failed validation, so nothing changed on the volume.

**Your options**
1. **Resize and raise IOPS together (needed for 20,000 IOPS):**
   `aws ec2 modify-volume --volume-id <vol-id> --size 20 --iops 20000`
   - The modification should go from `modifying` to `optimizing` to `completed`. The new settings apply once it reaches `optimizing`.
   - Cost goes up, because you pay for both the added GiB and the added IOPS.
   - Size can't be reduced later. You can change IOPS back afterwards, but each change counts toward the limit of 4 modifications per volume in 24 hours.
   - Take a snapshot first if the data matters.
2. **Stay at 15 GiB:** set `--iops 15000` or lower. This is the cheaper option and needs no file system work.

**After a size increase, extend the file system.** Run these on the instance:
- `lsblk` to find the device and partition.
- `sudo growpart /dev/<device> <partition-number>`, only if the volume has a partition.
- `sudo xfs_growfs -d <mount-point>` for XFS, or `sudo resize2fs /dev/<device-or-partition>` for ext4.

**What I couldn't check**
- I didn't find a 15 GiB io2 volume in us-east-1 in this agent space's account (012345678901_1). If your volume is in another Region or account, give me the volume ID and Region.
- I did see one earlier modification in this account: vol-1234567890abcdef0_24 went from 15 GiB / 15,000 IOPS to 20 GiB / 20,000 IOPS and completed on 2026-09-18. I can't confirm it's your volume.
- Before you go to 20,000 IOPS, check that the attached instance's EBS baseline IOPS and throughput can support it. Volumes on one instance share that limit, so I need the instance to check it.
- Check your Region's io2 IOPS quota in Service Quotas too. A request within the per-volume limit can still fail on the regional quota.
- I didn't query CloudTrail, so I can't tell you how many of the 4 modifications in 24 hours remain.

If you send the volume ID and Region, I can check the instance baseline and quota headroom. I can then submit the `--size 20 --iops 20000` change for your approval.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
